sections.title: Fixed-Köhler Illumination
sections.description: Why removing an adjustment step matters in a classroom.
body: Köhler illumination is the standard for even, glare-free microscope lighting, and getting it right normally takes a trained hand: aligning the condenser, centering the field diaphragm, adjusting for each new sample. In a research lab, that is a five-minute task for someone who does it daily. In a classroom of thirty students on their first day with a microscope, it is thirty separate failure points before anyone has actually looked at a cell.

Primostar 1 removes the step entirely. The illumination arrives pre-fixed, so image quality does not depend on whether the last student to use the microscope set it up correctly. A teacher hands the microscope over already working.

faqs.answer: It is an upright microscope built for clinical and biomedical laboratory routine work, including hematology, histology, cytopathology, and general clinical microscopy, with built-in Smart Microscopy documentation.

faqs.question: What is Smart Microscopy?
faqs.answer: A documentation system that captures a true-color, correctly scaled image with a single press of the Snap button, without needing a separate computer or software.

faqs.question: Does scaling get added automatically?

faqs.question: Can it handle fluorescence imaging?

faqs.question: What makes it ergonomic?

faqs.question: Can it track samples by barcode?

faqs.question: Is a two-person shared view available?

faqs.question: How does Eco-mode work?
faqs.answer: Axiolab 5 automatically goes to standby after 15 minutes of inactivity, saving energy without needing to be switched off manually.

faqs.question: How is Axiolab 5 different from Primostar 3?
faqs.answer: Primostar 3 is built primarily for teaching and basic routine lab work. Axiolab 5 is positioned specifically for clinical and biomedical laboratories, with Smart Microscopy documentation, dedicated ergonomic features, and co-observation options Primostar 3 doesn't offer.

longForm.heroLead: Multichannel fluorescence used to mean a workstation, manual channel switching, and exposure settings adjusted by hand between every wavelength. Axioscope 5 collapses all of that into one press. Pair it with the Colibri 3 LED light source and the Axiocam 203 mono camera, select the channels for UV, blue, green, and red excitation, and press Snap. The system switches wavelengths, adjusts exposure automatically, acquires each channel, and hands back a single overlaid multichannel image with a scale bar already included, even without a PC connected. The same Smart Microscopy logic runs through brightfield work too. Focus, press Snap, done. Color appears in the captured image exactly as it looked through the eyepieces, brightness and white balance adjusted automatically. Ergotubes adapt eyepiece height and angle to natural posture, every essential control sits within easy reach, and the light manager adjusts illumination automatically, no manual lamp brightness dialing between samples. What it replaces: manual channel switching and PC-based fluorescence documentation. What it adds over Axiolab 5: true multichannel fluorescence, up to four channels in one click. Where it sits in the range: below Axioscope 7's motorized whole slide imaging, above routine brightfield-only microscopes.
